title: An Impala Can Leap 33 Feet in a Single Bound

scenes.text: An impala can leap 33 feet in one bound.
It can also jump about ten feet straight up.
Impalas live in Africa, where lions, leopards and cheetahs hunt them.
When danger comes, they often flee through or over the bushes.
That jumping is their best defence.
Thirty-three feet long. Ten feet high. All in one leap.

description:
An impala can leap about 10 metres, or 33 feet, in one bound, and about 3 metres, or 10 feet, straight up.
That jumping is its best defence against lions, leopards and cheetahs.
How far can you jump? Comment below.
first_comment: 33 feet in one bound. How far can you jump on your best day?
